title: His pace slackened. Here. Am I going to aunt Sara’s or not?
html_source:
This prompts relatively long thoughts/memories of aunt Sara’s. The unsuspecting reader may assume he’s gone there but the memories are sandwiched either side of

‘Am I going to Aunt Sara’s ?’ and

‘He halted. I have passed the way to Aunt Sara’s. Am I not going there ? Seems not.’

Without prompts from others, Stephen cannot enact a visit – his day is a series of happenings rather than actions (Morris, Veteran and Virgin Readings of Ulysses).

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Simon Dedalus does not take his son’s identity as an artist seriously and criticizes both Stephen’s position and his relationship with his Aunt Sally by saying, “Couldn’t fly a bit higher than that eh?” (38). Simon’s critcism of his dead wife’s family becomes most intrusive in the statement, “O weeping God the things I married into.”
Really pretty dreadful guy.
